protocol.study: Publication-disjoint sensitivity analysis of the previously published ChEMBL 37 measured-affinity snapshot
protocol.data: experiments/v3/affinity_curated.json, unchanged 468 rows; CC BY-SA 3.0; results already explored under v3 scaffold split, so this is robustness analysis rather than new external confirmation
protocol.components: Globally union rows sharing any nonempty document_id; for document_and_scaffold also union shared non-isomeric scaffold (including ACYCLIC). Rows lacking document IDs excluded with count. Shared molecules across targets are unioned in both schemes.
protocol.split: Component key = SHA256 of newline-joined sorted unique standardized SMILES. SHA256('dmease-affinity-v4|'+component_key), first eight hexadecimal digits modulo 100: <70 train, <85 validation, else test. No rebalancing or seed search.
protocol.selection: Minimum validation MAE; stable ties. Save all validation scores and selected checkpoint hash before test predictions. Report all candidates, never select on test.
protocol.metrics: Per target and Ki/Kd separately: MAE, RMSE, R2, Spearman; train-test document, compound, scaffold overlap. Insufficient strata remain unevaluated. Bootstrap selected-minus-mean MAE by connected components (2000 repeats seed42).
limits: Small number of publications may make all fixed splits insufficient
Document isolation does not remove assay heterogeneity
Document-only splitting can share scaffolds and must report this
No whole-herb affinity or clinical efficacy interpretation
